title: External Knowledge Infusion for Tabular Pre-training Models with Dual-adapters

problem.claim: Tabular pre-training models need to better understand semantic entities in tabular data despite their surrounding irregular non-semantic content.

gap.claim: Existing solutions are built directly on tabular data, while external knowledge injection must overcome substantial structural and content differences between external knowledge and tabular data.

contributions.claim: A dual-adapter framework is inserted into a pre-trained tabular model to enable flexible and efficient external knowledge injection.
Parallel adapters are trained using knowledge-graph triplets and semantically augmented tables for knowledge infusion and alignment with tabular data.
A path-wise attention layer fuses cross-domain representations using weighted contributions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The framework was extensively tested across five application scenarios covering zero-shot and fine-tuning-based tabular understanding tasks at the cell, column, and table levels.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tabular pre-training models are increasingly used for tabular data analysis.
Existing approaches operate on mixed semantic and non-semantic tabular content, although semantic entities are a small but important portion of tables.
The paper seeks to inject common-sense knowledge from external sources, while addressing domain gaps between external knowledge and tabular data.
The proposed framework uses dual adapters trained on knowledge-graph triplets and semantically augmented tables, followed by path-wise attention for representation fusion.
The framework is tested across five application scenarios and multiple tabular understanding settings and levels.

source_observation.claim: Semantic entities may be a minority component of tabular data while remaining important for table understanding.

interpretation.claim: Representation learning for tables may benefit from explicitly isolating or strengthening semantically meaningful content.

application.claim: When designing tabular models, consider separate mechanisms for semantic content rather than treating all cell content uniformly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy improves every tabular dataset or task.

source_observation.claim: External knowledge and tabular data differ substantially in structure and content.

interpretation.claim: Knowledge transfer across domains may require explicit alignment mechanisms rather than direct injection.

application.claim: For cross-domain knowledge integration, use separate adaptation or alignment components before fusing representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which domain gaps are most difficult or when dual adapters are necessary.

unknowns: No quantitative results or comparison outcomes are reported.
The abstract does not specify the external knowledge sources, datasets, baselines, or adapter architecture details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, reproducibility, or generalization beyond the reported scenarios.
